subject: general
question: According to the Census of India 2011, ‘Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)’ comprise how much of the population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**7.9 million**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, 'Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)' comprise 7.9 million people.
 
• The ORP category includes those who do not identify with the six major religions listed in the census data: Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• These religions include smaller faiths and tribal religions practiced in various regions across India.
 
• This category helps in recognizing the diversity of beliefs and practices present in the country, reflecting the pluralistic nature of Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, but the first complete and synchronous census was conducted in 1881.
 
• The census collects data on population size, distribution, and various socio-economic parameters such as literacy, employment, and housing.
 
• The latest census was conducted in 2011, and the next one was scheduled for 2021 but was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **Religion Data in Census**
 
 
• The religion data in the Indian Census includes information on various religious communities in the country.
 
• The major religions accounted for in the census are Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• In addition to these, the census also recognizes 'Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)' and 'Religion not stated' categories.
 
• This data helps in understanding the religious composition and diversity of the Indian population.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Census Data**
 
 
• Census data is crucial for planning and policy-making by the government.
 
• It helps in the allocation of resources, development of infrastructure, and implementation of various welfare schemes.
 
• It also provides valuable insights for researchers and demographers studying population trends and socio-economic changes.
 
• Accurate census data is essential for ensuring effective governance and equitable distribution of services.
